families.axis: merely liable to sin → wicked past any reform

members.gloss: morally bad in principle or practice
members.tone: The plain, unhedged moral verdict, and it covers both the settled principle and the actual practice rather than choosing between them.
Names the thing as vice itself rather than describing a fault in it, which makes it absolute where *wicked* is merely damning.
Presents vice as the settled bent of the thing, so it sounds like a diagnosis of character beside *evil*'s flat sentence.

members.gloss: (of an actor or role) being or playing the villain
members.tone: A casting word: it marks the villain's part, or the actor filling it, and condemns nobody.
Formal and heavy-syllabled, delivering the same extreme-and-criminal verdict as *heinous* in a more elevated register.
The blunt public condemnation, wickedness pitched so far into the criminal that the word works almost as a sentence.

members.gloss: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin
members.tone: The gravest of its group, weighing the wrong as an enormity rather than simply logging it as sin like *sinful*.

members.gloss: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin
members.tone: The plainest naming of wickedness-as-sin, condemnatory without the swell of *iniquitous*.

members.gloss: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin
members.tone: Measures the wickedness as distance from godliness, so the fault is a standing away rather than *sinful*'s committed offence.
Pictures reform as recovery and denies it — nothing here can be got back.
The heaviest of these four, since redemption is what it withholds: a final verdict rather than a prognosis.
The same refusal built on a blunt negative prefix, more workaday in sound than *irredeemable*.
States only that reform will not take, a practical verdict without *irredeemable*'s sense of a soul past saving.
Condemns the wickedness in the abstract, where *villainous* points instead at the one committing it.
Casts the extreme wickedness as a villain's, making it a fact of character rather than of the deed.
Concedes only that sin is possible, not that any has been done, where *sinful* finds the wrong already there.

families.axis: a passing freshening → the imparting of life itself

members.tone: The plain, full-strength word for the effect, and the only one here that promises strength as well as liveliness, where *enlivening* offers spirit alone.
Warm approval aimed at spirit rather than muscle - what it gives is vivacity, not the strength *invigorating* claims.
The same gift of spirit as *animating*, but framed as a lift applied to something that was flat before.
Approval with a bite in it - the energy arrives sharply, where *refreshing* delivers the same energy gently.
Mild and matter-of-fact praise that renders vitality as pace and snap rather than as depth of force.
The simplest word in the group for this energy, crediting clarity and cleanness with the lift that *bracing* wins by sharpness.
Easy, grateful approval - the energy it names reads as relief from tiredness rather than as a charge of power.
Identical in force to *refreshing* but stiffer in build, which lends the same lift a formal weight.
Cool, measured approval that credits a thing with steadying and energizing rather than delighting, unlike the showier *exhilarating*.
The high end of the family - the lift goes past energy into open cheerfulness, which *stimulating* stops short of.
Cooler than *exhilarating* for the same effect, naming the rousing of liveliness and good cheer without saying how high it rises.

members.gloss: giving or having the power to give life and spirit
members.tone: The most absolute claim available here, since what it grants is life and spirit outright rather than a boost to either.

members.gloss: giving or having the power to give life and spirit
members.tone: The same gift of life and spirit as *life-giving*, stated as a working effect rather than as the grand attribute.

members.gloss: tending to impart new life and vigor to
members.tone: Approval for a lift that is a return of something lost - new life and vigor given back, not given for the first time as in *life-giving*.

members.gloss: tending to impart new life and vigor to
members.tone: Names the same power of return as a settled property of the thing, calmer and more formal than the active *renewing*.

families.axis: plain vitality → spirits fizzing over into speech

members.tone: The plain measure of the family — life and energy stated without a metaphor attached, so every other member here is a way of colouring it.

members.gloss: (often followed by ‘with’) full of life and spirit
members.tone: Credits life and spirit rather than motion, and leans on a following 'with' to name whatever the thing is brimming over with.
Liveliness as vigorous springing action — sturdier and more robust than *bouncy*, which makes the same spring sound weightless.
The spring taken as a temperament rather than a feat — lighter and more playful than *bouncing*.
Informal and brisk — lively action as a snap of energy, with none of the dignity *spirited* carries.
The dignified member: lively action with mettle and will behind it, where *peppy* is only pep.
Informal, and here the lively action is speed — quickness rather than the buoyancy of *bouncy*.
Puts freshness beside the animation, so the liveliness comes across as light and easy where *spirited* comes across as strong.

members.gloss: full of or showing high spirits
members.tone: Covers both being full of high spirits and showing them, naming the outward fizz and the inward supply at once.

members.gloss: marked by high spirits or excitement
members.tone: High spirits or excitement caught in the act of rising — a thing in motion where *bubbly* names a settled quality.

members.gloss: marked by high spirits or excitement
members.tone: The polished word for the same fizz — high spirits or excitement described with a formality the shorter members refuse.

members.gloss: marked by high spirits or excitement
members.tone: The weakest approval of the fizz: the high spirits or excitement are granted, but froth lets them look light and easily dispersed.

members.gloss: marked by high spirits or excitement
members.tone: The brightest of the set — high spirits or excitement that flash and dazzle rather than merely bubble.

members.gloss: marked by high spirits or excitement
members.tone: The same flash in a smaller, prettier register — decorative where *scintillating* is dazzling.
Moves the fizz into the voice: enthusiasm uttered with nothing holding it back, warm but with an ear on the overflow.
Names the quality of that unrestrained enthusiasm rather than a burst of it — looser and more casual than *burbling*.
